feedback.problem: Find the first four non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\frac{1}{1+3{x}^{4}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard Maclaurin expansion for $\frac{1}{1-x}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1-x} & =1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-3{x}^{4}$ in the above expansion and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1+3{x}^{4}} & =\frac{1}{1-(-3{x}^{4})} \\  & =1+(-3{x}^{4})+{(-3{x}^{4})}^{2}+{(-3{x}^{4})}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =1-3{x}^{4}+9{x}^{8}-27{x}^{12}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
